scenarios.name: Clean login + extraction
scenarios.description: No chaos. Fresh login, then extract stats and odds.

scenarios.name: Existing session reuse
scenarios.description: The browser starts with a valid saved session; the agent should reach the data without seeing the login form.

scenarios.name: Expired session re-login
scenarios.description: A saved session is force-expired server-side; the agent must notice the redirect and log in again.

scenarios.name: Cookie banner blocks table
scenarios.description: A consent banner overlays the page and intercepts clicks until accepted.

scenarios.name: Modal overlay blocks table
scenarios.description: A newsletter modal appears shortly after load and must be dismissed to reach the content.

scenarios.name: Delayed table render
scenarios.description: Tables render client-side behind a skeleton after a seeded 1.5–4s delay.

scenarios.name: Network slowdown
scenarios.description: Every response is delayed by a seeded 0.5–2.5s latency.

scenarios.name: CSS class drift
scenarios.description: All CSS class names carry a seed-derived suffix; ids and data-testids are removed.

scenarios.name: Changed column order
scenarios.description: Stats table columns are deterministically permuted.

scenarios.name: DOM layout change
scenarios.description: Stats render as a card grid instead of a table; odds switch to a stacked list.

scenarios.name: Hidden tab required
scenarios.description: Season stats live behind a non-default tab that must be clicked first.

scenarios.name: Pagination required
scenarios.description: The stats table shows 5 rows per page; the rest require clicking Next.

scenarios.name: Partial data missing
scenarios.description: A few cells render as em-dashes; extraction should degrade gracefully with explicit warnings, not fail.

scenarios.name: Page copy changes
scenarios.description: Headings, labels and button text are swapped for synonyms between runs.

scenarios.name: Odds format variation
scenarios.description: Odds display as American moneyline (+120 / -145) instead of decimal and must be normalised.

scenarios.name: Stale session mid-flow
scenarios.description: The session is invalidated server-side after the first authenticated page view; the agent is bounced to login between the stats and odds pages and must recover.

scenarios.name: Corrupt data → validation failure
scenarios.description: The page serves malformed values (negative played, inconsistent W/D/L, unparseable odds). Correct behaviour is a clean, categorised validation failure — not silently bad data.

scenarios.name: Site version 1 (launch)
scenarios.description: The stat site exactly as every engine's author first saw it: stable ids, one standings table, decimal odds. The clean baseline the survival curve starts from.

scenarios.name: Site version 2 (content refresh)
scenarios.description: A routine content pass: headings and button labels are reworded and the stats columns are reordered. No rebuild — but positional selectors now read the wrong column.

scenarios.name: Site version 3 (redesign)
scenarios.description: A full front-end rebuild: hashed CSS classes, ids gone, copy reworded, and the standings move from a table to a card grid. Only structure-blind reading still gets through.

scenarios.name: Blocked and slow
scenarios.description: A consent banner and a newsletter modal both block the page while the tables render late behind throttled responses — four obstacles stacked on one clean dataset.

scenarios.name: Session churn
scenarios.description: The session drops between the stats and odds pages, the standings span three paginated views, and odds arrive as American moneyline: recover, page through, and normalise.

scenarios.name: Messy data day
scenarios.description: A newsletter modal over a slow page hiding partial data — several cells render as em-dashes. Correct behaviour is to dismiss, wait, and degrade with explicit warnings, not fail.

scenarios.name: Redesign storm
scenarios.description: Everything a redesign throws at once: hashed classes with ids removed, reworded copy, and a card-grid layout. Only semantic reading gets through it unaided.
